# f5xc_nat_policy (Resource)

NAT Policy object represents the configuration of Network Address Translation parameters on<br>F5XC Customer Edge sites. The following properties can be configured in this object:<br>Site where the NAT objects are applicable<br>Ingress points where the NAT policies need to be applied<br>Match criteria of the packet to apply NAT Policy<br>Action to take if the Match criteria passes

To get more information about f5xc_nat_policy, refer:

- [API documentation](https://docs.cloud.f5.com/docs-v2/api/nat-policy)

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example: Nat Policy - Full

resource "f5xc_securemesh_site_v2" "site" {
  name      = "example-nat-site-x8bgfj-164000"
  namespace = "system"

  logs_receiver_choice = {
    logs_streaming_disabled = true
  }

  blocked_services_choice = {
    block_all_services = true
  }

  provider_choice = {
    kvm = {
      orchestration_choice = {
        not_managed = {}
      }
    }
  }
}

resource "f5xc_nat_policy" "example" {
  name        = "example-nat-policy"
  namespace   = "default"
  description = "Full NAT policy example"

  labels      = { env = "example", owner = "network" }
  annotations = { owner = "platform-team" }

  applies_to_choice = {
    site = {
      refs = [{ name = f5xc_securemesh_site_v2.site.name, namespace = f5xc_securemesh_site_v2.site.namespace }]
    }
  }

  rules = [
    {
      name          = "example-rule-full"
      enable_choice = { enable = true }
      scope_choice  = { node_interface = {} }

      criteria = {
        protocol_choice = {
          udp = {
            source_port      = { port_match_choice = { port_ranges = "1000-2000" } }
            destination_port = { port_match_choice = { port = 53 } }
          }
        }
        network_choice   = { site_local_network = true }
        source_cidr      = ["10.20.0.0/16"]
        destination_cidr = ["172.16.0.0/12"]
      }

      action = {
        source_nat_choice = {
          dynamic = {
            pool_choice = {
              pools = {
                prefixes      = ["192.168.20.0/24"]
                ipv6_prefixes = ["fd48:fa09:d9d4:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000/48"]
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### Required

- `name` (String) name This is the name of configuration object. It has to be unique within the namespace. It can only be specified during create API and cannot be changed during replace API. The value of name has to follow DNS-1035 format.
- `namespace` (String) namespace This defines the workspace within which each the configuration object is to be created. Must be a DNS_LABEL format. For a namespace object itself, namespace value will be ''

<a id="nestedatt--rules--action"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.action`

Optional:

- `source_nat_choice` (Attributes) NAT Choose between source NAT or Virtual Subnet NAT (Static NAT). When a match occurs, source NAT will change the original source address to either an SNAT Pool for East-West Scenarios or Cloud Elastic IP Object when traffic is destined to the internet. Virtual Subnet NAT is a static NAT implementation that changes the source & destination address and is mostly used for overlapping address scenarios.<br>Exactly one of `dynamic` or `virtual_cidr` must be specified when `source_nat_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--action--source_nat_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--rules--action--source_nat_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.action.source_nat_choice`

Optional:

- `dynamic` (Attributes) Source NAT Source NAT to either an SNAT Pool for East-West traffic or to a Cloud Elastic IP Object. Note that for a 3-node cluster the IPv4 prefix list should provide a minimum of 3 addresses to ensure each node gets an IP address from the pool.<br>Conflicts with `virtual_cidr`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--action--source_nat_choice--dynamic))
- `virtual_cidr` (String) Virtual Subnet NAT Virtual Subnet NAT is static NAT that does a one-to-one translation between the real source IP CIDR in the policy and the virtual CIDR in a bidirectional fashion. The range of the real CIDR and virtual CIDRs should be the same (e.g. if the real CIDR has the CIDR 10.10.10.0/24, the virtual CIDR has 100.100.100.0/24.<br>Conflicts with `dynamic`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an `import` block to import this resource by ID.

> **Note:** Replace placeholder values (for example, `<namespace>`, `<name>`) with actual values.

#### Command-Line Import

Use the following `command` to import this resource from the command line:

```shell

```
